title.narrative: Adaptive management and restoration of degraded Aleppo pine forest in the Kasserine governorate (Tunisia) to strengthen resilience to climate change, conserve biodiversity, improve productivity and food security

description.narrative: 1. Local communities are at the heart of the project's approach. Greater involvement of forest populations in decision-making processes and natural resource management will both promote conservation and support sustainable economic activities, adapted to local realities. The development of diversified, resilient and biodiversity-friendly value chains, such as rosemary, honey and Aleppo pine seeds (Zgougou), will help generate stable incomes, particularly for women and young people, who are priority target groups for the project. By meeting local needs for NWFPs and ecological services, these actions will also contribute to food security in a region marked by high levels of rural poverty.2. The project's interventions will enable communities to become full players in the sustainable management of their environment. The participatory elaboration of the CDP based on the medium-term revised forest management plans will foster their ownership of resources and reduce potential conflicts related to the use of forest resources. These processes will also reinforce the participatory identification of equitable and sustainable management practices, ensuring inclusive access to the socio-economic benefits of forest landscapes while maintaining their ecological functions3. Local communities, with a focus on young people and women, will benefit from technical, institutional and entrepreneurial capacity building. The project will support the structuring of forestry GDAs, the creation of silvicultural microenterprises and the establishment of productive partnerships with the private sector. It will establish the governance, monitoring and technical support mechanisms needed to ensure the sustainability of participatory approaches beyond the project's lifecycle.4. The restoration practices promoted under the project - such as ANR, rangeland rotation, erosion control and integrated NWFP management - will help improve soil and water resource conservation, with direct benefits for human health and the local environment. Protecting and restoring Aleppo pine ecosytems will help maintain essential ecosystem services like biodiversity, and preserve a healthy living environment for rural communities.5. Finally, In response to the the effects of CC (prolonged drought, fires, insect pests), the production systems promoted by the project will strengthen local resilience, thanks to income diversification. The project will also contribute to CC mitigation through the fight against land degradation.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Restore and manage degraded Aleppo pine forest ecosystems in the Kasserine governorate by developing and implementing adaptive, integrated and participatory management tools to build resilience to CC, preserve biodiversity, halt and reverse degradation and maintain productivity.
